paths.description: Homepage and global shell: news landing, navigation, consent, responsive states, performance, security, privacy, accessibility and memory.
Politics listing archetype representing section/index templates.
Current subscriber article representing article/detail and paywall treatment.
Question/search surface and attempted query journey.
Prominent subscription landing representing commercial choice, pricing and commitment disclosure. Checkout/payment was not entered to avoid a transaction.
Deliberately invalid URL representing HTTP 404 recovery.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is byte-identical to the default capture (124,352 bytes), and the DOM reports color-scheme: normal with a white body background.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and retint surfaces, text, imagery and browser chrome with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Loading animations continue under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirmed the preference and still found four running skeleton/skeletonShimmer animations, each with a 1,600 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential skeleton shimmer under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and retain only static progress cues.

findings.summary: Navigation swaps are abrupt rather than using progressive-enhanced View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The captured DOM/CSS contains no view-transition rule or declaration across a multi-page news experience.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-origin cross-document View Transitions with a no-motion fallback and stable transition names for shared header/article elements.

findings.summary: Long news pages lack a scroll-state progress or responsive chrome cue.
findings.evidence: The homepage is about 32,000 CSS px tall, but captured CSS/DOM contains no scroll-state query or progress indicator; navigation chrome remains static.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading/scroll progress cue and use scroll-state container queries where supported, with a static fallback.

findings.summary: Menus and transient panels do not expose CSS anchor-positioning/fallback placement.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no anchor-name, position-anchor or position-try use despite menu and panel controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for transient menus/tooltips while preserving the existing fallback layout.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures the entire first viewport on every representative page.
findings.evidence: Desktop and 360 px screenshots of home, section, article and search show a large modal covering the headline or task, with additional sticky subscription chrome on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the full-content-blocking first-load wall with a compact, accessible consent surface; keep reject/continue controls equally visible and allow content reading without an interruption.

findings.summary: The consent surface is an iframe-based custom modal rather than a document-native dismissible primitive.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found an iframe titled “Consent window”; the document contains no dialog element, while the blocking surface is rendered outside the document’s semantic controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a correctly labelled dialog for modal consent, manage focus and Escape, and use popover only for non-modal settings.

findings.summary: Mobile content is crowded by stacked consent, subscription and fixed navigation chrome.
findings.evidence: At 360×800 the consent surface, red subscription banner and bottom navigation leave no usable article content in the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove stacked promotions while consent is open and reserve persistent chrome for one high-value control surface at a time.

findings.summary: Responsive behaviour is viewport-led rather than component-led.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe reports container-type: normal and captured CSS contains no @container rule, although cards are reused in many widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable card/list regions and size/style container queries, preserving media-query fallbacks.

findings.summary: Some navigation targets are too short and focus treatment is weak.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found many 22 px-high navigation links and only a 1 px dotted focus outline; Lighthouse also failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Give interactive targets at least 24×24 CSS px spacing (prefer 44 px for primary touch controls) and a clearly visible :focus-visible ring.

findings.summary: The page purpose and next action are hidden on first visit.
findings.evidence: Across home, section, article and search mobile captures, the consent wall obscures the page heading and primary content/task.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the heading and primary task visible, and move consent to a non-obscuring, equally actionable surface.

findings.summary: Consent blocks the representative search journey before the user can ask a question.
findings.evidence: The search page contains a labelled question textarea and submit action, but its first viewport is fully covered by consent; a direct ?question=agriculture URL does not execute or prefill the query.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow the search form to be used without advertising consent, preserve the query in the URL, and show a clear loading/result state after submission.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 10.7 s, FCP 4.2 s, TTI 16.5 s and performance 0.63; the independent trace measured LCP 2.57 s under a lighter desktop-like run, confirming strong condition sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP content, defer consent/ad/analytics work, reduce render-blocking dependencies and validate against mobile field-like conditions.

findings.summary: A very long main-thread task blocks responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded a 664.93 ms longest task and 651.11 ms total blocking time across three long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the 665 ms task, split non-critical work, schedule by priority and delay ad/analytics initialisation until after content interaction readiness.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is dominated by scripts and a large dependency graph.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 225 requests and 2.54 MB transferred, including 86 scripts/1.95 MB and 91 stylesheets; multiple parser-inserted high-priority scripts originate in the document head.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate styles, defer non-critical scripts, gate ad/analytics bundles, and shorten the critical dependency chain.

findings.summary: Third-party and duplicated tag-manager work dominates the JavaScript budget.
findings.evidence: Five Google tag-manager/gtag resources account for roughly 1.39 MB, while third-party requests account for 109 requests and 2.02 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tag containers, audit each vendor for user value, and load optional integrations conditionally after consent.

findings.summary: Core carousel and bottom-navigation semantics are invalid.
findings.evidence: axe found critical required-parent/required-children and invalid aria-controls failures, unnamed listboxes and three unnamed carousel-dot buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace conflicting menu/listbox roles with native list/button semantics or complete the required ARIA pattern; name every control and fix aria-controls targets.

findings.summary: Several text labels fail WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: axe measured examples at 4.29:1, 2.84:1 and 1.6:1, including ad labels, game titles and the TV-grid label.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to at least 4.5:1 for normal text and verify all image-overlay states.

findings.summary: ARIA structure undermines focus and reading order.
findings.evidence: axe reported critical invalid menubar/menuitem parenting, list items under a non-list role and nested interactive descendants; focus styling is only a 1 px dotted outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer native navigation lists, remove redundant menu roles, avoid nested controls, and provide a strong focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Some image assets have invalid sizing metadata.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio; the image primitive found 9 images without dimensions, 63 without srcset and 9 legacy-format images among 100 inspected.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct intrinsic aspect ratios, add width/height, and provide responsive source sets without distorting media.

findings.summary: The page requests notification permission on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed notification-on-start and traced the call to async-helpers JavaScript, before a user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Request notifications only after an explicit, contextual user action and explain the value before invoking the browser prompt.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but CSP and cookie protection are weak.
findings.evidence: Headers show CSP limited to upgrade-insecure-requests; fig_save_consent and Wysistat lack Secure, and all three observed cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive nonce/hash CSP and mark cookies Secure with the narrowest workable SameSite policy; review long-lived analytics cookies.

findings.summary: A large tracking footprint loads before advertising consent.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe saw 21 non-main origins and known Google, DoubleClick and Taboola trackers; HAR recorded 109 third-party requests/2.02 MB while analytics payloads state isConsentGiven=false.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential trackers until opt-in, minimise vendors and events, and batch first-party analytics.

findings.summary: Notification permission is requested out of context.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified a notification permission request during page load rather than following a user gesture.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate notification permission behind an explicit alert-subscription action; use capability explanation before the prompt.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are absent or incomplete.
findings.evidence: The main response lacks X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; CSP contains only upgrade-insecure-requests, though HSTS and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, a strict referrer policy, a least-privilege permissions policy and a real script/style CSP with frame-ancestors.

findings.summary: The French experience presents a mixed-language consent flow.
findings.evidence: Representative French pages declare lang=fr, but the blocking consent heading/body and “Continue without accepting” link are English while action labels are partly French.
findings.suggestedFix: Localise the entire CMP from the document locale and keep language consistent across iframe and host content.

findings.summary: Consent choices use asymmetric visual emphasis.
findings.evidence: “ACCEPT ALL” and setup are large filled buttons, while “Refuse all” is plain text at the bottom and “Continue without accepting” is a small top link; the modal blocks content.
findings.suggestedFix: Give accept and reject equal prominence, use one language, avoid blocking content, and preserve easy settings/reversal.

findings.summary: Image delivery leaves avoidable responsive-format waste.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 63 lack srcset, 66 below-fold images were not marked lazy and 9 use legacy formats; 9 lack dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, add srcset/sizes and dimensions, and lazy-load genuinely below-fold media.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics perform substantial work before consent.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 109 third-party requests and 2.02 MB third-party transfer, while the trace reports 651 ms blocking time and tracker calls indicate consent=false.
findings.suggestedFix: Prevent optional fetches before consent and interaction, deduplicate tags, and deprioritise background measurement.

findings.summary: Third-party code is disproportionate to the first-view news content.
findings.evidence: Third parties transfer 2.02 MB of the 2.54 MB load; tag manager, ad-tech and recommendation scripts are the largest offenders.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce a third-party byte/request budget, remove redundant vendors and defer non-essential media/ad code.

taskList.title: Replace the blocking, asymmetric consent wall and prevent all non-essential tracking before opt-in
Cut the critical JavaScript and third-party dependency chain to restore mobile LCP and responsiveness
Repair carousel, navigation and list semantics, contrast, focus and target sizing
Deploy a restrictive CSP and complete cookie/header defenses
Modernise responsive image delivery and intrinsic sizing
Respect dark mode and reduced motion preferences
Localise the consent experience consistently in French
Move notification permission behind an explicit user action
Progressively enhance navigation with View Transitions, scroll-state cues and anchored overlays
Adopt component-level container queries for reused card/list layouts
